first_impression.reaction: Googled 'who can perform a marriage' because my partner's brother keeps saying he'll 'just get ordained online' and marry us. First paragraph gives me a date stamp, the rule and the four types. That's the answer. Then a Concierge link in paragraph two before anything's been proved, which put my guard up. I went straight to the FAQ, then the friend or family section, the register check and the overseas bit. Section 41 of the Act, AGD links, the actual register URL, the 6 month assessment window. All stuff I can check myself, and the Justice of the Peace answer is exactly the kind of catch I'd want flagged. Reads like a reference page with a planner bolted on at the end, which is fine by me.

journey.section: Intro
journey.quote: As at November 2026, you must be married by an authorised marriage celebrant to be legally married here.
journey.reaction: Dated and blunt. That's the rule I came for, in one line.

journey.section: Intro
journey.quote: When the legal side is settled, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=who-can-perform-a-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration.
journey.reaction: Sales link in paragraph two, before the page has shown me a single source. It's conditional so it's minor, but evidence first, then the ask.

journey.section: Who can legally perform a marriage in Australia?
journey.quote: Section 41 of the Act is headed "Marriages to be solemnised by authorised celebrant".
journey.reaction: An actual section number and heading. I can look that up in two minutes. Good.

journey.section: Who can legally perform a marriage in Australia?
journey.quote: AGD keeps a database of all authorised marriage celebrants, so you never have to take anyone's word for it.
journey.reaction: That's the attitude I want. Don't trust us, check the register.

journey.section: Types of authorised marriage celebrants
journey.quote: The two Commonwealth types share one regulator and one register, which is why they are sometimes grouped as a single type, with three groups in all.
journey.reaction: I'd have found 'three' on another site and wondered which one was wrong. They've pre-empted that. Took me a second read, but it's honest.

journey.section: Commonwealth-registered marriage celebrants
journey.quote: There are over 10,000 of them in Australia.
journey.reaction: A number. Dated by the section above it. Fine.

journey.section: State and territory officers
journey.quote: A registry wedding suits couples who want the legal marriage done simply, often ahead of a larger celebration elsewhere.
journey.reaction: 'Often' according to whom? Probably true, but it's an assertion in a section that's otherwise all regulation.

journey.section: Can a friend or family member marry you?
journey.quote: Timing is the part couples underestimate.
journey.reaction: Unsourced generalisation. The 6 month figure right after it does the work; this line doesn't need to be there.

journey.section: Can a friend or family member marry you?
journey.quote: AGD has up to 6 months to assess a completed application, applications are assessed in the order received, and none can be fast-tracked.
journey.reaction: This is what I'll send the brother-in-law. Hard number, no fast track. Settles the argument.

journey.section: Can a friend or family member marry you?
journey.quote: If a sibling or close friend is set on it, raise it well over a year before the wedding, because the notice must also reach the celebrant at least one month before the day.
journey.reaction: Six months plus one month is seven. Where does 'well over a year' come from? Presumably the Certificate IV takes time too, but the page never says how long, so the maths doesn't add up on the page.

journey.section: How to check your celebrant is authorised
journey.quote: Check before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: Practical and on my side, not theirs. After the vendor I got burnt by, this is exactly the order I'd do it in.

journey.section: How to check your celebrant is authorised
journey.quote: Each entry shows the registration status (for example "Registered" and "Active"), the registration date, and either "Civil Ceremonies" or a religious marriage celebrant label.
journey.reaction: Tells me what I should actually see on screen. That's a checkable step, not a promise.

journey.section: How to check your celebrant is authorised
journey.quote: One more thing to know early: celebrants should not give advice on migration matters such as prospective marriage or spouse visas.
journey.reaction: A limit stated plainly, with who to go to instead. Good.

journey.section: What your celebrant must do to make it legal
journey.quote: The ceremony must include specific words.
journey.reaction: Which words? The page says they're required and then doesn't tell me what they are or where to read them.

journey.section: Witnesses and signing
journey.quote: If an error on a certificate is found after the ceremony, it can be corrected only while the couple and witnesses are still present.
journey.reaction: That's a real catch. The kind of thing nobody tells you until it's too late.

journey.section: Frequently asked questions
journey.quote: Being a Justice of the Peace is not one of the four types of authorised celebrant.
journey.reaction: Exactly the misconception I'd half believed. Straight answer, then 'check the register'.

journey.section: Who can marry you if your wedding is overseas?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, overseas marriages cannot be performed by an Australian-authorised marriage celebrant, and cannot be registered in Australia.
journey.reaction: Straight rule, no wiggle room. This is what actually decides our plan.

journey.section: Who can marry you if your wedding is overseas?
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments for the celebration abroad as your single point of contact, in your time zone and quoting in AUD, while the legal ceremony stays with you and your celebrant: speak with [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=who-can-perform-a-marriage&utm_content=secondary).
journey.reaction: They say what they don't do. A planner admitting the legal bit isn't theirs is worth more to me than a feature list. Still says 'payments' without saying whether they take a cut from those vendors.

journey.section: Planning the celebration
journey.quote: One Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, with the fee agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the right signal for my spreadsheet. It's the first thing on the page that speaks to my actual worry.

journey.section: Planning the celebration
journey.quote: Once you know who will marry you, and where the legal ceremony happens, the rest is the part your guests will remember.
journey.reaction: Brochure voice. Harmless, I skip it.

unanswered_questions: What are the specific words the ceremony must include, or where exactly can I read them? The page says they're required but doesn't show them.
How long does the Certificate IV in Celebrancy usually take? Without it, 'well over a year' isn't backed by anything on the page.
If we marry legally at home and celebrate abroad, can a non-registered friend or family member lead the overseas celebration, since it carries no legal weight? The page implies it but never says it.
For the split route, does the Wedded Advisor help line up the legal ceremony date with the celebration abroad, or is that on us?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from venues or vendors it handles payments for? (deferred business detail)
Is there a real wedding you've planned on the 'legal at home, celebrate abroad' route, with the actual budget?

turn_offs_found.quote: When the legal side is settled, [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=who-can-perform-a-marriage&utm_content=primary) can take on the celebration.
turn_offs_found.why: A CTA in the second paragraph, before any evidence. It's conditional so it's minor, but I came for a legal answer and got a sales link before the sources.

turn_offs_found.quote: Timing is the part couples underestimate.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsourced generalisation on a page that otherwise cites everything. It's padding, and padding makes me wonder what else is.

turn_offs_found.quote: A registry wedding suits couples who want the legal marriage done simply, often ahead of a larger celebration elsewhere.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Often' with nothing behind it. An opinion dressed as a fact in a section that's otherwise straight regulation.
'Most couples' says who? It's probably sensible advice, but it's presented as data it doesn't have.

turn_offs_found.quote: Once you know who will marry you, and where the legal ceremony happens, the rest is the part your guests will remember.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional sales copy instead of facts. It's the tone I skip past to find the actual terms.

would_share_with: My partner's brother, the 'Can a friend or family member marry you?' section, because the 6 month assessment with no fast track ends the 'I'll just get ordained online' idea
My partner, the Justice of the Peace FAQ and the register check steps, before we pay any celebrant deposit

cta_reaction.why: The page earned credit: dated, sourced, sends me to the government register instead of asking me to trust them, and says plainly the legal ceremony isn't theirs. 'Fee agreed in writing before any work begins' is the right line. But I came here to settle a family argument about who can marry us, not to hire a planner, and my real question, whether they take a cut from the vendors whose payments they handle, isn't answered. They go in the comparison spreadsheet; I wouldn't enquire off this page alone.

top_3_changes: Move the intro Concierge link below the key takeaways or into the overseas section, so the facts come before the ask: 'When the legal side is settled, Wedded Concierge can take on the celebration.'
Cut or source the unsupported generalisations: 'Timing is the part couples underestimate.', 'Most couples keep it simpler.' and 'often ahead of a larger celebration elsewhere'.

Back up 'raise it well over a year before the wedding' with the qualification time if a source has it, and either state the required ceremony words or link to where they're published, instead of only saying 'The ceremony must include specific words.'

Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection

No invented brand facts; commission and real-budget questions placed in unanswered_questions as deferred
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold the prescribed ceremony words (or an AGD link to them) and a typical Certificate IV duration? Either would close a gap the sceptic flagged.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via Google for 'who can perform a marriage' while comparing three planners, looking to settle whether a relative can marry them, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood is 2.
No prices and no celebrant names are deliberate and not penalised; the celebrant's certificate cost is the celebrant's matter, not the brand's.
The 5-minute budget covered the intro, FAQ, friend or family, register check and overseas sections in full and a skim of the rest.
